study type: Observational study / Case series with risk factor analysis
exposure: Fetomaternal disease (hazard of preterm birth, preeclampsia, gestational toxicosis, subcompensated placenta dysfunction, placental abruption, anemia)
Exacerbation of chronic pyelonephritis during pregnancy
Phlebeurysm of lower limbs in mothers
Maternal burdened heredity of cardiovascular system (heart rhythm and conductivity disorders)
outcome: Heart rhythm disorders (sinus bradycardia, extrasystole, atrial flutter, QT prolongation syndrome)
cohort: The study included 384 newborns aged 0-8 days, with a mean gestational age of 39.2+/-1.7 weeks, who presented with clinical signs of cardiovascular system issues, among whom 37 were diagnosed with heart rhythm disorders.
finding: The development of heart rhythm and conductivity disorders in newborns is associated with various unfavorable ante- and perinatal factors, including pathological pregnancy and delivery, with 97.3% of patients showing heart rhythm normalization by 7.2+/-2.9 days of age.
mod_finding: 72.9% (p<=0.05) of infants with heart rhythm disorders were born by Caesarian section.
